title: Super New Kuroda carrot (Super Kuroda): Characteristics
metaDescription: Super New Kuroda carrot is an open pollinated carrot variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Super New Kuroda carrot is an open pollinated carrot variety, also sold or known as Super Kuroda. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Super New Kuroda carrot is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Super Kuroda, this is the same carrot. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [carrot variety finder](/crop-varieties/carrot), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).
Key facts about Super New Kuroda carrot

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit carrot fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** About 105 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Root: orange to dark orange, about 17 cm long and 4 to 5 cm wide, 230 to 260 g.
Even roots that pull out easily.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: ramgo's Kuroda type carrot, listed first on its professional carrot line, the only evidence found is Ramgo's listing. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual carrot on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Super New Kuroda carrot

Carrot is a highland crop in the Philippines. Pick a root length your soil can hold: short types for heavy soil. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Super Kuroda the same as Super New Kuroda?
items.a: Yes. Super Kuroda is another name for Super New Kuroda. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Super New Kuroda?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
